comments.author: @Donadoni-f3j
comments.text: I live in East Java and have experienced eruptions of Mount Kelud on three occasions: once as a teenager in 1990, and twice as an adult in 2007 and 2014. The most powerful eruption occurred in 2014; there was a rain of ash and sand, and lightning flashed across the sky accompanied by booming thunder, even though we were 70 kilometers away from the eruption site. Many roofs collapsed under the weight of the sand, and the air felt hotter than usual. Since the eruption took place at night, the lightning in the sky was clearly visible—a sight that was both terrifying and fascinating. The volcanic ashfall extended as far as the provinces of Central Java and Yogyakarta, more than 500 kilometers away.
